title: Candidate decoding label law
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet $	ext{Fin}(q)$, let each vertex $v$ have a finite candidate set $C_v\subseteq \text{Fin}(q)$, and choose a default label $a_0\in\text{Fin}(q)$. For each vertex, the candidate decoding label law is the probability mass function obtained by applying the finite-candidate law to $C_v$ and $a_0$.
hypotheses_covered: A regular unique game $G$ with alphabet size $q$
A finite candidate set for each vertex
caveat: The definition of the finite-candidate probability law is not included, so its precise distribution cannot be stated.
